target.title: fix(sdk): add prototype-pollution guard to migration config merge (#103059)
target.body:
## Summary

- Add `isBlockedObjectKey` guard to `mergeMigrationConfigValue` and `writeMigrationConfigPath` in `src/plugin-sdk/migration.ts`.
- Reject `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` keys before they reach bracket assignments, matching the guard already used by the sibling config-path writer.

## What Problem This Solves

The migration-import config merge helpers had no prototype-pollution guard. A crafted or tampered prior-tool config file imported through `openclaw onboard`'s migration flow that contains a map entry named `__proto__` could trigger prototype pollution. This is the sixth instance of this bug class in the repo; the other five files were already fixed.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Prototype pollution from imported config files is prevented. The guard is consistent with the sibling `parseConfigPath`/`setConfigValueAtPath` that already rejects blocked keys.
- **What did NOT change:** Normal config migration continues to work. Only `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` keys are now silently dropped.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** Uses the same `isBlockedObjectKey` from `src/infra/prototype-keys.js` that protects the sibling config-path writer.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #103059. The issue reports that migration config merge has no prototype-pollution guard, unlike the sibling config-path writer.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

No overlapping PRs found.

## Evidence

- Source inspection confirms `isBlockedObjectKey` is now called in both `mergeMigrationConfigValue` and `writeMigrationConfigPath`.
- The same guard is used in `src/config/config-paths.ts:42` (`parseConfigPath`).
- Format clean (oxfmt).

Fixes #103059
